correctness.rationale: Surjective restriction of finite-group characters to the cyclic step subgroup yields precisely h frequencies per root label. For a nowhere-zero signal the edge ratios telescope to one around each m-cycle. All-good cycles require alpha^m times the label product to equal one; a unique bad edge is allowed iff alpha^(m*m)≠1; at least two bad edges can be constructed while avoiding finite forbidden cosets. The complete coefficient construction proves all quantifiers, the exact labelled pattern counts and both sharp minima. Exact rational and independent direct DFT checks cover 139968 cyclic labelled candidates and 403 noncyclic product-group witnesses but are supplementary to the proof.

originality.rationale: Full published mathematical statements closest to this claim concern sparse-window minimum support for a fixed coordinate set, prime-cyclic two-sparse pair cardinalities, generic-window two-point signals, or phase retrieval from magnitudes. The 2006 foundational STFT uncertainty paper and later 2014/2022 endpoint equality studies do not state the all-subsets if-and-only-if labelled root-coset classification. A proof ingredient overlaps strongly with the equal-weight result but does not imply the new arbitrary-weight m²-torsion transition, per-label product condition and all-group enumeration. Broad semantic and formula searches found no covering formulation; unindexed equivalences remain a realistic priority risk.
residual_risks: The closest published equal-weight cyclic proof uses related cancellable-edge reasoning; an unstated easy variation of that proof could overlap some subcases.
An older unindexed graph-holonomy or support-pattern classification could imply the exact labelled enumeration.
Literature searching does not prove priority and no independent audit has occurred.

value.rationale: This determines a natural complete feasible-zero-pattern invariant of a two-tap Gabor measurement on every finite abelian group, retaining the locations and character labels that minimum-support inequalities discard. A nontrivial global cycle-holonomy constraint produces an exact resonance/nonresonance transition and closed pattern counts; it can guide which erased time-frequency coefficients can arise structurally. The result is not merely an arbitrary small finite lookup, a renaming, or an epsilon improvement; no stability or general-filter claims are made.
